title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation system was used to create non-consensual sexual imagery of a real person without her knowledge or permission. The system itself had no built-in safeguard against this use, though it is not established whether such safeguards existed in the tool deployed or were simply not applied. The deployment failure was complete: the technology was used in the open to cause harm to a specific individual.

The attacker obtained source photographs from the victim's social media accounts, generated explicit deepfake images using AI, and distributed them across multiple platforms through anonymous accounts while making threats. Catching this would have required either the AI system to refuse the request, the social media platforms to detect and remove the content, or a human reviewer to intercept it at any point in the chain. None of these happened.

It is not established what AI system was used, what its stated purpose was, or whether it had been designed or configured to prevent non-consensual intimate imagery.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and distributing artificial intelligence-generated obscene images of a college acquaintance. Bansal obtained photographs from the woman's private social media account and used AI technology to create explicit morphed images. He then circulated this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using various Gmail addresses to hide his identity. The woman discovered the harassment when she received messages from anonymous accounts informing her that her manipulated photographs and videos were being shared across Discord servers, along with threatening messages intended to humiliate her.

Police launched an investigation after the 22-year-old victim filed a complaint at the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi. Investigators analyzed digital footprints and traced connections between the fake social media accounts and email addresses to identify Bansal. During interrogation, he admitted to knowing the victim from college and revealed that personal resentment had motivated his actions following repeated insults between them. He also disclosed that after he initially uploaded the content, other unknown users created additional explicit AI-generated material that he subsequently reposted. Police recovered a mobile phone, two SIM cards, and other digital evidence related to the case, with investigation continuing.
